title: Clear the dead mark on both heartbeat paths and repoint the decline text
action: Per D8 the dead mark is reversible, and it must clear on BOTH heartbeat writers, not whichever is convenient. There are two, each with its own heartbeat_session taking the sessions lock and writing last_heartbeat: hooks/state_sync.rs:494 (PostToolUse, SubagentStop, Stop) and hooks/prompt_context.rs:1597 (UserPromptSubmit). A session that comes back by typing a prompt renews through the second one, so covering only the first ships a half-revival whose test still goes green. In each writer, inside the existing Acquired(guard) closure that already holds the sessions lock (state_sync.rs:498-505 and the matching block at prompt_context.rs:1597-1606), when the record being touched carries status dead: remove status and dead_at and set revived_at to the touch time. revived_at holds only the most recent revival. Add no new lock — the closure already holds the sessions lock — and change neither the throttle nor the fail-open Busy arm. Then repoint the D6 decline text: the user-visible string is the blockers line at orient.rs:268, which points at bee cells claim-next because bee recovery scan did not exist when it shipped; it now names bee recovery scan, and that command runs. Two comments repeat the same now-false claim that claim-next is the sweep's only trigger, at orient.rs:193 and orient.rs:238 — correct both, or the source keeps asserting something the code disproves. Write one test per heartbeat writer: a test that exercises only one path is not evidence for the other.

truths: A record carrying status dead loses status and dead_at and gains revived_at when the PostToolUse/Stop heartbeat touches it
The same holds when the UserPromptSubmit heartbeat touches it, proved by its own test
The heartbeat throttle and the fail-open busy-lock arm are unchanged on both paths
orient's decline text names bee recovery scan, and that command runs
No comment in orient.rs still claims claim-next is the sweep's only trigger

artifacts.substantive: the clearing step inside the existing locked closure; no new lock
the same clearing step in the second writer

key_links: both heartbeat_session implementations clear the mark inside the lock they already hold
prohibitions: No new lock acquisition on either heartbeat path
No change to the heartbeat throttle or to the fail-open busy arm
No FIX or blocker line naming a command that does not run
